title.narrative: Stöd till UNIDO för en analys av kakaomarknaden i DRK
Support to UNIDO for Market Study on cacao in DRC

description.narrative:
The contribution focuses on supporting UNIDO in the DRC with the aim of obtaining a diagnostic study of the cocoa value chain in the provinces of Kongo central, Kwango and Kwilu.
This study provides a good understanding of the current situation and development possibilities by emphasizing the place of women and young people in the sector; it demonstrates how support to the sector can create new opportunities and innovations that could facilitate the creation and development of micro and small industries / cooperatives, job creation and increased income for households, man, women and Youth.
It also sets the conditions for reducing deforestation due to shifting cultivation. Specific objective (results): A diagnostic study of the development of the cocoa sector and its current situation which highlights the potential of the sector to significantly increase the incomes of women and young people and to preserve the environment.
At the end of the Agreement, UNIDO will formulate and present a diagnostic study of the potential development of the cocoa sector that incorporates stakeholder contributions.

The study has shown that the cocoa sector is a growing sector with untapped potential, from which growers, actors of all value chains (men, women and young people) could benefit and improve their income. a sustainable way. For this, it is necessary to support the planters on the axes of:
Quality of production, with monitoring from nurseries to plantations, their management and maintenance. Revitalization of old plantations and the establishment of an agroforestry system that meets the needs of local populations and respect for the environment Transformation of wet beans into commercial cocoa: with the installation of a simple fermentation tank and an adequate and decentralized drying system. Organization of the export sector, with support in identifying chocolate makers interested in purchasing high quality cocoa. Establishment of a circular system of the cocoa value chain which recovers the waste from cocoa plantations and allows the creation of energy and composting, Setting up of a small chocolate factory which should help to create a local market in the capital or the towns, while promoting employment. Here again, an approach linked to entrepreneurship on a circular model could create many jobs for young people and women. Sustainable coexistence of cocoa plantations and surrounding protected areas.
At the same time, it is necessary to work with the Government on the regulatory and fiscal framework, and to support quality infrastructure so that the state system comes to support the export sector.
A project on the cocoa value chain as a whole would revitalize cocoa planting areas and could thus have an impact on farmers, their families and villages for inclusive development that respects social and environmental standards.
